title: Sunwicks Creek (Astoria)
summary: Sunwicks is a creek at Astoria in Queens, near Hell Gate on Long Island.
history_content: The creek appears in a 1664 deed to William Hallet, where the boundary began at the first creek called Sunwick below Hell Gate.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Sunwick, Sunwicks, and Sunswicks. The name is interpreted as stone-house, perhaps referring to a Dutch or English stone building near the creek.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names reinforce an intimate relationship with the land, convey a broad range of knowledge such as travel routes and traditional hunting and fishing grounds, and are touchstones for history and legends.”

— Geographical Names Board of Canada, Stories from the Land: Indigenous Place Names in Canada (n.d.), opening overview

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Sunwicks keeps a Queens creek name visible within the dense colonial record landscape around Hell Gate and Hallets Point.
